dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN, chosen by the owner on 23 November 2026 and amended the same night with the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted (4 in 1798), and the others are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (a target, not a quota); one affair's items are handled as in X-1800-01; the eligible items not chosen are listed here.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1798 has 8 catalogue series, which are 8 papers. The Gazette (Portland) survives from April, the Virginia Argus in 10 issues, the Wilmington Mercury in September and October and the Eagle of Hanover in 2 issues; 4 to 8 papers are in print in any three weeks, so an item needs 4 papers, and 5 in the weeks when all 8 are in print.

dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1798 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 387 items, 83 in 4 or more papers by the finder's count), and the families of 1797 were looked for on the 1798 pages (items_from_1797.json). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by machine by about 100 words of its text from the finder's position, over all 1,656 pages in both transcriptions (a dense run of its word 5-grams, at least a quarter of them); the counts were joined into documents where two items stand at the same place on the same pages, or where two documents titled by the same opening stand on mostly the same pages. Every item the machine put in every surviving paper, and the news considered for choosing, was counted again by about 70 words from its own opening, the acts of Congress by their first section's own words (counts_1798.json), and every page found was read; the bills printed before the acts they became, in other words, are counted apart. Each admitted printing was checked against its page scan.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted by their own words, 43 items of 1798 are eligible: 29 in 4 papers, 12 in 5, 2 in 6, 0 in 7. 4 items are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 21 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news (one affair's items under a parent story, X-1800-01). 11 more eligible items counted by their opening are not chosen, and 6 documents of the item finder are eligible by their own words and not chosen; all are listed with their counts. 5 candidates counted by their opening are below the bar and listed. 172 more documents of the item finder are below the bar by their own words (docs_1798.json); they are not listed one by one. The bills counted apart from their acts, the act printed in full by one paper and the documents of the item finder that stand at the enacting formula are listed as read.
counted_item_by_item.Titles of the items not chosen: Each eligible document of the item finder not chosen is listed by its own words: the dateline or heading before the finder's position and the words that follow (some begin inside the item, where the finder's position does); a notice or advertisement that names a private person is described instead (R-04). Each candidate counted by its opening is listed by a title of the review's.

for_user_decision.The papers in print and the bar (X-1798-: 8 catalogue series, 8 papers; the Gazette (Portland) survives from April, the Virginia Argus in 10 issues, the Wilmington Mercury in September and October and the Eagle in 2 issues; 4 to 8 papers are in print in any three weeks, so an item needs 4 papers, and 5 in the weeks when all 8 are in print.
for_user_decision.Choosing among the eligible items (X-179: As built (B1): 4 items printed by every surviving paper are admitted, and 21 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news: the President's messages and the Treasury's circular on the envoys' dispatches, the proclamation of a fast, the acts and motions of Congress on France and on aliens and sedition, the letters of Mr. Gerry and the French minister, General Washington's acceptance, the war in Europe and Egypt, and the Senate's answer to the President's speech: 19 stories in 29 groups. The other eligible items are not chosen and are listed with their counts.
for_user_decision.The acts of Congress counted by their fi: As built (C-02): the acts open with the enacting formula ('BE it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives ...'), so counts by their opening reach every act's pages; each act was counted again by its first section's own words, and the pages were read. Documents of the item finder that stand at the formula are listed with a note that their machine counts reach other acts.
for_user_decision.A bill counted apart from its act (X-179: As built (X-1809-07, X-1803-10): the Senate's bill more effectually to protect the commerce and coasts (3 papers), the Senate's bill to declare the treaties with France void (2 papers) and the House's bill to suspend the commercial intercourse with France (3 papers) are counted apart from the acts they became; the act declaring the treaties void is then in 3 of 5 papers and the act suspending the intercourse in 1, below the bar.
for_user_decision.One affair's items (X-1798-04): As built (X-1800-01): the envoys' dispatches (the President's messages of 5 March, 19 March and 3 April, and the Treasury's circular of 21 March), Mr. Gerry's correspondence with the French minister (the minister's letter of 12 July and Mr. Gerry's answer of 20 July), the action off the mouth of the Nile (the minute of facts and Rear-Admiral Nelson's letter) and the opening of the session in December (the President's speech of 8 December and the Senate's answer) are each a parent story with their separate public acts or documents as sub-stories.
for_user_decision.Printed again counts again (X-1798-05): As built (C-08): the Gazette of the United States printed the President's message of 5 March, the act to protect the commerce and coasts, Mr. Foster's resolutions and the minute of facts twice; each printing is in its group.
for_user_decision.One report in two forms (X-1798-06): As built: the Philadelphia report of the Delaware's capture of a French privateer is printed in two forms ('We have the satisfaction to announce ...' and 'Yesterday Capt. Decatur ... arrived at the Navy-Office. He informs ...'), sharing the account of the capture word for word; they are one item. The report from French papers on the envoys' dispatches stands inside a longer Boston report in four papers and alone in the Kentucky Gazette.
for_user_decision.Another text that shares the words (X-17: As built (C-07): Mr. Blount's resolutions on Great Britain, moved in the words of Mr. Foster's on France, are another text; an essay quoting a clause of the President's message of 3 April does not count as a printing. The Gazette of the United States of 30 November prints the act on sedition whole, from its heading to 'Approved, July 14th, 1798. JOHN ADAMS', inside an essay ('it will be expedient to recite it here from beginning to end'): a whole reprint inside commentary counts (X-1802-04), and the act is in 5 of the 8 papers that survive for its weeks with it (without it, 4 of 5): eligible either way.
for_user_decision.Items not chosen on reading (X-1798-08): As built: the King's answer to the two Houses of Parliament (4 of 5 papers) is not chosen because the Virginia Argus prints its opening at the foot of a page that has no RevX transcription; Mr. Gerry's answer to the corporation of Trenton (4 of 6) is not chosen because three of the four papers print an extract after their own words. Either can be added after a scan check.
for_user_decision.Headings above an item (X-1798-09): As built (as X-1794-09): an excerpt starts with the heading, dateline or date line printed directly above the item; a paper's own dateline, the dateline of the paper an act or a letter was taken from, a paper's own sentence introducing an item, the session's caption over an act ('Fifth Congress of the United States: at the second session ...', with 'LAWS OF THE UNITED STATES. By Authority.') and a country or section heading stay out and are noted.
for_user_decision.Titles of the items not chosen (X-1798-1: As built: every eligible item not chosen is listed by its own opening words; notices and advertisements are not chosen (C-10) and are described without the private persons they name (R-04); documents of the item finder that stand at an act's enacting formula are described, with a note that their machine count reaches other acts.
for_user_decision.Filing and dates (X-1798-11): Data: the release's map of misfiled RevX pages lists 27 pages of 1798, all of the New Hampshire Gazette (January to July), each holding the text of another page of the same issue; four of them hold printings of the ledger (4, 11 and 18 April, 8 May), whose excerpts come from the CA transcription.
